description: Library of common undergraduate organic transformations. Each entry is a reaction SMARTS template (or a list of them) plus the reagents, catalysts, solvents and conditions it needs. 'triggers' lists the functional-group ids that make the template relevant (a list of lists for two-component reactions). 'selectivity' names a ranking rule from selectivity.py; 'site' and 'other' are atom-map numbers in the product template. 'cautions' are chemoselectivity warnings shown when another group is present ({group} is replaced by the group name). 'example' is used by the test suite.

transformations.name: PCC oxidation of a primary alcohol to an aldehyde
transformations.mechanism: Chromate ester formation, then E2-like elimination
transformations.conditions: Room temperature, anhydrous. With no water present the aldehyde hydrate cannot form, so oxidation stops at the aldehyde.

cautions.message: {group} in the molecule will also be oxidised (to a ketone).
{group}: thiols are oxidised by Cr(VI) as well.

transformations.name: Jones oxidation of a primary alcohol to a carboxylic acid
transformations.mechanism: Oxidation to the aldehyde, hydration, then oxidation of the hydrate
transformations.conditions: 0 °C to room temperature. The aqueous acid hydrates the intermediate aldehyde, which is then oxidised further.

cautions.message: {group} will also be oxidised (to a ketone).
{group} will also be oxidised to a carboxylic acid.
{group}: Jones usually leaves C=C intact, but KMnO4 (the alternative) would cleave it.

transformations.name: Oxidation of a secondary alcohol to a ketone
transformations.mechanism: Chromate ester formation, then elimination
reagents: PCC or Jones reagent (CrO3, H2SO4, H2O)
transformations.conditions: Room temperature. Ketones resist further oxidation, so both mild and strong Cr(VI) reagents stop here.

cautions.message: {group} will also be oxidised (to an aldehyde with PCC, to an acid with Jones).

transformations.name: Pinnick oxidation of an aldehyde to a carboxylic acid
transformations.mechanism: Chlorous acid adds to the carbonyl, then fragments
transformations.conditions: Room temperature. Mild conditions that leave alkenes and most other groups alone.

transformations.name: NaBH4 reduction of an aldehyde to a primary alcohol
transformations.mechanism: Nucleophilic hydride addition, then protonation
transformations.conditions: 0 °C to room temperature, then aqueous workup.

cautions.message: {group} will also be reduced. Aldehydes react faster, so low temperature or NaBH(OAc)3 can give some selectivity.
{group} is left untouched by NaBH4, so this step is chemoselective.

transformations.name: NaBH4 reduction of a ketone to a secondary alcohol
transformations.mechanism: Nucleophilic hydride addition, then protonation
transformations.conditions: 0 °C to room temperature, then aqueous workup. An unsymmetrical ketone gives a new stereocentre as a racemate.
alternatives: CBS reduction for an enantioselective version

cautions.message: {group} will also be reduced, and faster than the ketone.
{group} is left untouched by NaBH4, so this step is chemoselective.

transformations.name: LiAlH4 reduction of an ester to two alcohols
transformations.mechanism: Hydride addition, loss of alkoxide, second hydride addition to the aldehyde
transformations.conditions: 0 °C, then reflux; careful aqueous workup (Fieser).
alternatives: DIBAL-H at -78 °C stops at the aldehyde (see red_dibal_ester)

cautions.message: {group} is also reduced by LiAlH4.

transformations.name: DIBAL-H partial reduction of an ester to an aldehyde
transformations.mechanism: A single hydride delivery; the tetrahedral intermediate is stable at -78 °C until workup
reagents: then H3O+ or Rochelle salt workup
transformations.conditions: -78 °C, strictly 1 equivalent. Warming up or excess reagent over-reduces to the alcohol.

cautions.message: {group} competes for DIBAL-H.

transformations.name: LiAlH4 reduction of a carboxylic acid to a primary alcohol
transformations.mechanism: Deprotonation, then hydride delivery through an aldehyde intermediate
transformations.conditions: 0 °C, then reflux. The first equivalent of hydride is used up deprotonating the acid.
alternatives: BH3·THF - selective for acids over esters

cautions.message: {group} is also reduced by LiAlH4.

transformations.name: LiAlH4 reduction of an amide to an amine
transformations.mechanism: Hydride addition, loss of O-Al to give an iminium, second hydride addition
transformations.conditions: Reflux. The C=O becomes CH2 and the nitrogen is kept.

cautions.message: {group} is also reduced by LiAlH4.

transformations.name: LiAlH4 reduction of a nitrile to a primary amine
transformations.mechanism: Two successive hydride additions to C#N
transformations.conditions: 0 °C to reflux. Gives R-CH2-NH2.

cautions.message: {group} is also reduced by LiAlH4.

transformations.name: Wolff-Kishner deoxygenation of a ketone or aldehyde (C=O to CH2)
transformations.mechanism: Hydrazone formation, base-mediated loss of N2
transformations.conditions: Heat to about 200 °C, strongly basic. Use Clemmensen for base-sensitive substrates.

cautions.message: {group} would be hydrolysed under the hot KOH conditions.
{group} may eliminate or be substituted under the hot basic conditions.

transformations.name: Reduction of a nitro group to an amine
transformations.mechanism: Stepwise electron and proton transfers (nitroso, then hydroxylamine, then amine)
transformations.conditions: Reflux. The base workup frees the amine from its ammonium salt.

cautions.message: {group} survives Sn/HCl but would be reduced by the H2/Pd-C alternative.

transformations.name: Catalytic hydrogenation of an alkene
transformations.mechanism: Syn addition of H2 on the metal surface
transformations.conditions: Room temperature, 1 atm H2. Syn addition; benzene rings and C=O are not reduced under these conditions.

cautions.message: {group} is also fully reduced.
{group} is also reduced to an amine under H2/Pd.

transformations.name: Full hydrogenation of an alkyne to an alkane
transformations.mechanism: Two successive syn additions of H2
transformations.conditions: Room temperature. The alkene intermediate is not isolated.

cautions.message: {group} is also reduced.
{group} is also reduced to an amine.

transformations.name: Lindlar reduction of an alkyne to a cis-alkene
transformations.mechanism: Syn addition of one equivalent of H2 on a poisoned catalyst
catalysts: Lindlar catalyst (Pd/CaCO3 poisoned with Pb(OAc)2 and quinoline)
transformations.conditions: Room temperature. The poisoned catalyst stops at the alkene, which is the cis (Z) isomer.

transformations.name: Na/NH3 reduction of an internal alkyne to a trans-alkene
transformations.mechanism: Single-electron transfers through a radical anion and a vinyl radical; the trans geometry is preferred
transformations.conditions: -78 to -33 °C. Gives the trans (E) alkene.

cautions.message: {group} would be deprotonated by NaNH2 formed in situ, not reduced.

transformations.name: Hydrobromination of an alkene (Markovnikov)
transformations.mechanism: Electrophilic addition through the more stable carbocation
transformations.conditions: 0 °C to room temperature, no peroxides. Br ends up on the more substituted carbon. Watch for carbocation rearrangements (hydride or methyl shifts).
alternatives: HCl gives the chloride; HI gives the iodide

transformations.name: Radical hydrobromination of an alkene (anti-Markovnikov)
transformations.mechanism: Radical chain: Br· adds first to give the more stable carbon radical
transformations.conditions: Radical conditions put Br on the less substituted carbon. This works only for HBr (not HCl or HI).

transformations.name: Acid-catalysed hydration of an alkene (Markovnikov)
transformations.mechanism: Protonation to the more stable carbocation, then water attack
transformations.conditions: Mild heating. The equilibrium can run backwards (dehydration); rearrangements are possible.

transformations.name: Oxymercuration-demercuration of an alkene (Markovnikov, no rearrangement)
transformations.mechanism: Mercurinium ion, water opens it at the more substituted carbon, then NaBH4 replaces Hg with H
transformations.conditions: Room temperature. Markovnikov alcohol with no carbocation rearrangement. Mercury is toxic.
alternatives: Alkoxymercuration (ROH instead of H2O) gives ethers

transformations.name: Hydroboration-oxidation of an alkene (anti-Markovnikov, syn)
transformations.mechanism: Concerted syn addition of H-B (B goes to the less hindered carbon), then oxidation with retention
transformations.conditions: 0 °C to room temperature. OH on the less substituted carbon; H and OH are added syn; no rearrangement.

cautions.message: {group} can be reduced by borane.

transformations.name: Bromination of an alkene (anti addition)
transformations.mechanism: Bromonium ion, then backside attack by Br-
transformations.conditions: Room temperature, in the dark. Anti addition gives the vicinal (trans) dibromide. The orange colour disappears - a classic test for unsaturation.

cautions.message: {group} also adds Br2.
{group}: electron-rich arenes may be brominated as well.

transformations.name: Bromohydrin formation (Br2 / H2O)
transformations.mechanism: Bromonium ion opened by water at the more substituted carbon
transformations.conditions: Room temperature. Anti addition; OH on the more substituted carbon. Base then closes the epoxide.

transformations.name: Epoxidation of an alkene with mCPBA
transformations.mechanism: Concerted 'butterfly' oxygen transfer (stereospecific, syn)
transformations.conditions: 0 °C to room temperature. The alkene geometry is kept (cis alkene gives cis epoxide). More electron-rich alkenes react faster.

cautions.message: {group} may undergo Baeyer-Villiger oxidation with excess peracid.
{group} is oxidised by peracids (N-oxide or hydroxylamine).

transformations.name: Syn-dihydroxylation of an alkene (OsO4 / NMO)
transformations.mechanism: Concerted [3+2] cycloaddition to an osmate ester, then hydrolysis
transformations.conditions: Room temperature. Syn addition gives the cis-1,2-diol.

transformations.name: Ozonolysis of an alkene (reductive workup)
transformations.mechanism: [3+2] cycloaddition to the molozonide, rearrangement to the ozonide, reductive cleavage
transformations.conditions: -78 °C (until a blue colour persists), then reductive workup. Cleaves C=C into two C=O (aldehydes and/or ketones).
alternatives: Oxidative workup (H2O2) turns aldehyde fragments into carboxylic acids

cautions.message: {group} is also cleaved (to carboxylic acids).

transformations.name: Mercury-catalysed hydration of a terminal alkyne (Markovnikov) to a methyl ketone
transformations.mechanism: Markovnikov addition of water to give an enol, which tautomerises to the ketone
transformations.conditions: Mild heating. Keto-enol tautomerism gives the methyl ketone.

transformations.name: Hydroboration-oxidation of a terminal alkyne to an aldehyde (anti-Markovnikov)
transformations.mechanism: Syn hydroboration with a bulky borane, oxidation to an enol, tautomerisation
transformations.conditions: 0 °C to room temperature. A bulky borane prevents double addition.

transformations.name: Alkylation of a terminal alkyne (acetylide SN2)
transformations.mechanism: Deprotonation by NaNH2, then SN2 on a primary alkyl halide
transformations.conditions: -33 °C (liquid NH3). Only methyl and primary halides; secondary and tertiary halides undergo E2 instead.
alternatives: n-BuLi in THF for the deprotonation
transformations.partner_hint: Add a primary alkyl halide as a second component, e.g. '<your alkyne>.CBr'.

transformations.name: Acid-catalysed dehydration of an alcohol (Zaitsev)
transformations.mechanism: E1 through a carbocation (2° and 3°); E2 for 1°
transformations.conditions: Heat (3°: ~25-80 °C; 2°: ~100-140 °C; 1°: ~170-180 °C). Distil off the alkene to push the equilibrium. Expect the more substituted alkene and possible rearrangements.

cautions.message: {group}: primary alcohols need harsh conditions and may rearrange or form ethers instead.

transformations.name: Conversion of a 1° or 2° alcohol to an alkyl bromide (PBr3)
transformations.mechanism: Activation as a phosphite ester, then SN2 by Br- (inversion)
transformations.conditions: 0 °C. SN2 with inversion at a stereocentre; no rearrangement.

transformations.name: Conversion of a 1° or 2° alcohol to an alkyl chloride (SOCl2)
transformations.mechanism: Chlorosulfite ester, then SN2 by Cl- when pyridine is present
transformations.conditions: 0 °C to reflux. The by-products SO2 and HCl are gases, which drives the reaction.

cautions.message: {group} will also be converted to the acyl chloride.

transformations.name: SN1 conversion of a tertiary alcohol to an alkyl bromide (HBr)
transformations.mechanism: Protonation of OH, loss of water to a 3° carbocation, Br- attack
transformations.conditions: Room temperature. Fast, through a carbocation (racemises a stereocentre). E1 alkene is a minor by-product.
alternatives: conc. HCl (+ ZnCl2) gives the tertiary chloride

transformations.name: Tosylation of an alcohol (makes a good leaving group)
transformations.mechanism: O-sulfonylation; the C-O bond is not broken, so configuration is retained
solvents: Pyridine (solvent and base) or CH2Cl2 / Et3N
transformations.conditions: 0 °C to room temperature. The tosylate can then do SN2 or E2 like a halide.

cautions.message: {group} would be sulfonylated (sulfonamide) as well.

transformations.name: Williamson ether synthesis
transformations.mechanism: Alkoxide (from NaH), then SN2 on a primary alkyl halide
transformations.conditions: 0 °C to room temperature. Put the bulky part on the alkoxide and keep the halide primary, or E2 takes over.
transformations.partner_hint: Add a primary alkyl halide as a second component, e.g. '<your alcohol>.CI'.

transformations.name: SN2 substitution of an alkyl halide by hydroxide
transformations.mechanism: SN2 (backside attack, inversion)
transformations.conditions: Warm. Best for methyl and primary halides; reactivity I > Br > Cl.

cautions.message: {group}: with a secondary substrate, E2 (alkene) competes strongly with hydroxide.
{group} would be saponified by NaOH.

transformations.name: SN2 substitution of an alkyl halide by cyanide (+1 carbon)
transformations.mechanism: SN2 (backside attack, inversion)
transformations.conditions: Room temperature to 60 °C. Adds one carbon; the nitrile can be hydrolysed (acid) or reduced (amine). NaCN is highly toxic.

cautions.message: {group}: secondary substrates react more slowly and E2 can compete.

transformations.name: SN2 substitution of an alkyl halide by azide
transformations.mechanism: SN2 (backside attack, inversion)
transformations.conditions: Room temperature to 80 °C. Azide is a weak base, so there is little E2. Reduce with LiAlH4 or H2/Pd to get a clean primary amine.

transformations.name: E2 elimination with a small base (Zaitsev)
transformations.mechanism: Concerted anti-periplanar E2
transformations.conditions: Heat. Small strong bases give the more substituted (Zaitsev) alkene, mostly E (trans).

cautions.message: {group}: primary halides mostly undergo SN2 (giving the ether) with NaOEt; use t-BuOK for elimination.

transformations.name: E2 elimination with a bulky base (Hofmann)
transformations.mechanism: Concerted E2; the bulky base removes the most accessible beta-H
transformations.conditions: Heat. The bulky base gives the less substituted (Hofmann) alkene and suppresses SN2.

transformations.name: SN1 hydrolysis of a tertiary alkyl halide
transformations.mechanism: Ionisation to a tertiary carbocation, then capture by water
solvents: H2O / acetone or aqueous EtOH (polar protic)
transformations.conditions: Warm, no strong base. E1 alkene forms alongside; a stereocentre racemises.
alternatives: AgNO3 in EtOH speeds up ionisation

transformations.name: Formation of a Grignard reagent
transformations.mechanism: Oxidative insertion of Mg(0) into the C-X bond (radical surface process)
transformations.conditions: Reflux under N2 or Ar. Any water or other acidic X-H destroys the reagent (R-MgX + H2O gives R-H).

cautions.message: {group} has an acidic H that will protonate (destroy) the Grignard reagent. Protect it first.
{group} is electrophilic and would react with the Grignard reagent as it forms.

transformations.name: Grignard addition to an aldehyde or ketone
transformations.mechanism: Nucleophilic addition of R-MgX to C=O, then acidic workup
transformations.conditions: 0 °C to room temperature. Formaldehyde gives a 1° alcohol, other aldehydes give 2° alcohols, ketones give 3° alcohols.
transformations.partner_hint: Combine the Grignard reagent with an aldehyde or ketone, e.g. 'CC[Mg]Br.CC(C)=O'.

transformations.name: Carboxylation of a Grignard reagent with CO2 (+1 carbon)
transformations.mechanism: Nucleophilic addition to CO2 to give a carboxylate, then protonation
transformations.conditions: Pour onto crushed dry ice, then acidify.

transformations.name: Conversion of a carboxylic acid to an acyl chloride
transformations.mechanism: Acyl chlorosulfite intermediate, then nucleophilic acyl substitution by Cl-
transformations.conditions: Reflux; SO2 and HCl are released as gases. Use the acyl chloride straight away (it is moisture-sensitive).

cautions.message: {group} will also react with SOCl2 (giving an alkyl chloride).

transformations.name: Fischer esterification
transformations.mechanism: Acid-catalysed nucleophilic acyl substitution (the alcohol oxygen ends up in the ester)
solvents: The alcohol itself, or toluene with a Dean-Stark trap
transformations.conditions: Reflux. This is an equilibrium (K ~ 1-10), so use excess alcohol or remove water. Tertiary alcohols do not work well.
transformations.partner_hint: Add an alcohol as a second component, e.g. '<your acid>.CCO'.

transformations.name: Saponification (basic hydrolysis) of an ester
transformations.mechanism: Hydroxide addition, loss of alkoxide; the acid-base step makes it irreversible
transformations.conditions: Reflux, then acidify to get the free carboxylic acid.

cautions.message: {group} may undergo SN2 or E2 with hydroxide.

transformations.name: Esterification of an acyl chloride with an alcohol
transformations.mechanism: Nucleophilic acyl substitution (addition-elimination)
transformations.conditions: 0 °C to room temperature. Fast and irreversible.
transformations.partner_hint: Add an alcohol as a second component, e.g. '<your acyl chloride>.CCO'.

transformations.name: Amide formation from an acyl chloride and an amine
transformations.mechanism: Nucleophilic acyl substitution (addition-elimination)
reagents: Et3N or pyridine (or 2 equiv of the amine)
transformations.conditions: 0 °C to room temperature.
alternatives: Carboxylic acid + amine + DCC or EDC (coupling agents)
transformations.partner_hint: Add a primary or secondary amine as a second component, e.g. '<your acyl chloride>.CN'.

transformations.name: Hydrolysis of an amide
transformations.mechanism: Nucleophilic acyl substitution under forcing conditions
transformations.conditions: Reflux for several hours; amides are the least reactive acid derivative. Gives the acid and the amine (as its ammonium salt in acid).

cautions.message: {group} will also be hydrolysed under these conditions.

transformations.name: Hydrolysis of a nitrile to a carboxylic acid
transformations.mechanism: Addition of water to give an amide, then amide hydrolysis
transformations.conditions: Reflux. Milder conditions can stop at the amide.

cautions.message: {group} will also be hydrolysed.

transformations.name: Acetal (1,3-dioxolane) protection of an aldehyde or ketone
transformations.mechanism: Acid-catalysed hemiacetal formation, then oxocarbenium ion, then ring closure
transformations.conditions: Reflux. The acetal is stable to bases, hydrides and Grignard reagents; remove it with H3O+ / acetone.

transformations.name: Wittig methylenation (C=O to C=CH2)
transformations.mechanism: Ylide addition, oxaphosphetane formation, loss of Ph3P=O
reagents: Ph3P=CH2 (made from Ph3P+CH3 Br- and n-BuLi)
transformations.conditions: 0 °C to room temperature. The new C=C forms exactly where the C=O was.

transformations.name: Reductive amination of an aldehyde or ketone
transformations.mechanism: Imine or iminium formation, then selective hydride reduction
transformations.conditions: Room temperature. NaBH3CN reduces the iminium faster than the C=O.
transformations.partner_hint: Add a primary or secondary amine as a second component, e.g. '<your ketone>.CN'.

transformations.name: Nitration of a benzene ring (EAS)
transformations.mechanism: Electrophilic aromatic substitution by the nitronium ion NO2+
transformations.conditions: 0-50 °C; keep it cold to avoid dinitration. The existing substituents decide where the nitro group goes.

cautions.message: {group}: in mixed acid the amine is protonated (anilinium is a meta director) and oxidised. Protect it as an acetanilide first.
{group}: phenols are oxidised by conc. HNO3. Use dilute HNO3 instead.

transformations.name: Bromination of a benzene ring (EAS)
transformations.mechanism: Electrophilic aromatic substitution by Br2 activated by FeBr3
transformations.conditions: Room temperature, in the dark.

cautions.message: {group} is so activating that polybromination happens with no Lewis acid (e.g. 2,4,6-tribromophenol).
{group} will add Br2 faster than the ring substitutes.

transformations.name: Chlorination of a benzene ring (EAS)
transformations.mechanism: Electrophilic aromatic substitution by Cl2 activated by a Lewis acid
transformations.conditions: Room temperature.

cautions.message: {group} will add Cl2 as well.

transformations.name: Sulfonation of a benzene ring (EAS, reversible)
transformations.mechanism: Electrophilic aromatic substitution by SO3 (or HSO3+)
transformations.conditions: Warm. Reversible: dilute H2SO4 and steam remove the SO3H group, so it can serve as a blocking group.

transformations.name: Friedel-Crafts acylation with acetyl chloride
transformations.mechanism: Electrophilic aromatic substitution by the acylium ion (no rearrangement, no polyacylation)
catalysts: AlCl3 (stoichiometric; it complexes the product ketone)
transformations.conditions: 0 °C to room temperature. The aryl ketone is deactivated, so only one acyl group goes on.
alternatives: Clemmensen or Wolff-Kishner afterwards gives a clean primary alkyl chain

cautions.message: {group}: strongly deactivated rings do not undergo Friedel-Crafts reactions.
{group}: the basic nitrogen complexes AlCl3 and shuts down the reaction.
{group}: if it sits on the ring, it deactivates it and Friedel-Crafts may fail.

transformations.name: Side-chain (benzylic) oxidation to a benzoic acid
transformations.mechanism: Radical oxidation at the benzylic C-H; the rest of the chain is cleaved off
transformations.conditions: Reflux. Needs at least one benzylic H (tert-butyl groups are not touched). Any alkyl chain becomes -COOH.

cautions.message: {group} is cleaved by hot KMnO4 as well.
{group} is oxidised as well.

transformations.name: Benzylic bromination with NBS
transformations.mechanism: Radical chain through the resonance-stabilised benzylic radical
transformations.conditions: Reflux or irradiate. NBS keeps the Br2 concentration low, so the ring is not brominated. Also works at allylic positions.

transformations.name: Sandmeyer bromination (Ar-NH2 to Ar-Br)
transformations.mechanism: Diazotisation to ArN2+, then Cu(I)-mediated radical substitution
transformations.conditions: Keep the diazonium salt cold (0-5 °C); it is unstable when warm or dry.
alternatives: CuCl gives Ar-Cl; KI gives Ar-I (no copper needed)

transformations.name: Sandmeyer cyanation (Ar-NH2 to Ar-CN)
transformations.mechanism: Diazotisation to ArN2+, then Cu(I)-mediated substitution
transformations.conditions: Cold diazotisation, then warm with CuCN. The aryl nitrile can be hydrolysed to a benzoic acid.

transformations.name: Diazonium hydrolysis to a phenol
transformations.mechanism: Diazotisation, then loss of N2 and capture of the aryl cation by water
transformations.conditions: Diazotise cold, then warm the aqueous solution.

transformations.name: N-Acetylation of an amine (acetamide)
transformations.mechanism: Nucleophilic acyl substitution on acetic anhydride
transformations.conditions: Room temperature. For anilines this tones down the NH2 (still an o/p director, but monosubstitution becomes possible). Remove with H3O+ or NaOH and heat.

cautions.message: {group} can also be acetylated (more slowly) with excess Ac2O.

transformations.name: Acid-catalysed hydrolysis of an epoxide (anti-1,2-diol)
transformations.mechanism: Protonated epoxide opened by water (SN2-like with SN1 character) with inversion
transformations.conditions: Room temperature. Anti opening gives the trans-1,2-diol from cyclic epoxides.

transformations.name: LiAlH4 opening of an epoxide (hydride at the less hindered carbon)
transformations.mechanism: SN2 by hydride at the less substituted carbon
transformations.conditions: 0 °C to room temperature. The OH stays on the more substituted carbon.

cautions.message: {group} is also reduced by LiAlH4.

transformations.name: Base-mediated opening of an epoxide by methoxide
transformations.mechanism: SN2 at the less hindered carbon (steric control)
transformations.conditions: Room temperature to reflux. The nucleophile attacks the less substituted carbon. Under acidic conditions (MeOH / H+) the regiochemistry flips to the more substituted carbon.
alternatives: Other nucleophiles: NaCN, NaN3, RMgX, R2CuLi
